thread.title: A Pandora Sale to SiriusXM Is Music to Investors’ Ears

author: David Marino-Nachison
title: A Pandora Sale to SiriusXM Is Music to Investors’ Ears
text:
Photo: Andrew Harrer/Bloomberg By David Marino-Nachison Updated Sept. 24, 2018 1:00 p.m. ET Listeners like the sound of Pandora Media ’s (ticker: P) tunes—and investors like the sound of Monday’s news of a deal to sell to SiriusXM Holdings (SIRI).
The deal comes as Pandora’s shares deliver big gains in 2018. The company faces stiff competition, but investors have backed management’s work increasing revenue , creative deals aimed at signing up subscribers , and timely acquisitions . Those factors, combined with an upbeat outlook for the year, have helped the stock rise nearly 90% through Friday’s close.
Still, it’s not shocking that Pandora wants to sell. While it’s been competitive in a space that includes not only Spotify Technologies (SPOT) but tech giants including Apple (AAPL) and Alphabet’s (GOOGL) Google and YouTube, the sale gives it a chance to quickly pump up the volume on growth.
Newsletter Sign-up As the announcement notes , SiriusXM already has more than 36 million subscribers; Pandora reported about 6 million at the end of the second quarter . The company, like much of its competition, believes bundles and family plans are an effective way to grow: They can be easier to sell, and consumers may be less likely to drop these subscriptions.
SiriusXM, meanwhile, clearly has reason to like the access to the streaming audience the deal provides. (Pandora, Apple, and Spotify are all components of the Barron’s Next 50 index .)
The merger has been brewing for some time. Back in May, we discussed public statements by Liberty Media (FWONA) CEO Greg Maffei—who is Pandora’s chairman—regarding the possibility of some kind of combination. (Liberty owns most of Sirius and some of Pandora.)
And my colleague Nicholas Jasinski foreshadowed it in June 2017, when SiriusXM invested in Pandora in the first place. (Full circle: That’s around the same time that Pandora sold Ticketfly to Eventbrite (EB), which recently had a hot IPO .)
According to Pandora and SiriusXM’s calculations, the offer represents a nearly 14% premium on a measure of recent average prices for the company’s stock. There’s still some daylight between Pandora’s current price and the offer value—about 7% at recent check—but a 14% gain from recent levels would mean the stock has more than doubled in 2018.
Recommended Reading Spotify and Pandora Are ‘Stronger Than Perceived’ Bundles Can Help Keep Subscribers Around Watch for a Verizon Deal for Sirius Pandora stock was up more than 4% on Monday morning. (SiriusXM’s shares were recently down more than 6%.)
“We have long viewed SiriusXM as the logical acquirer of Pandora,” Raymond James analysts wrote Monday. “We believe the modest premium reflects Sirius’s confidence that it is the primary bidder for Pandora.”
But even SiriusXM—and, by extension, Liberty—is willing to let someone with more money come along and shake things up. The deal includes a provision that lets Pandora hear, or even look for, a superior offer. With the merger scheduled to close in the first quarter, one might say it’s the final countdown.
